title: Oriental fruit moth on peach - China

Header: Oriental fruit moth on peach - China
Grapholita molesta syn. Cydia molesta , oriental fruit moth, ferskenvikler, 梨小食心虫 in Chinese

Prevention: Deep plough the soil around peach trees in autumn to reduce overwintering larvae.
Intercrop with chestnut to support natural enemy parasitic wasps.
Remove pruned branches and post-harvest fruits to decrease pests before winter.
Flood the soil with water about 70-100 cm on the ground for 3-5 days in winter to kill the overwintering larvae.
Monitoring: Start monitoring for larvae at flowering every 3 to 5 days.
Choose 10 out of 100 trees for monitoring.
Look on upper leaves, newly top twigs and young fruits for redish 1 to 1.5 cm soft larvae with dark head.
Leaves are distorted and wilt, twigs dieback due to larvae feeding.
Fruits may have several holes and gummosis exits.
Consider action when 10-15 percent of the peach trees have 10 to 20 larvae.
Lure adults with pheromone ((z)-8- twelve carbene-1-alcohol acetate) during
October at night to estimate peaks of moth populations and subsequent egg laying period.
At 15 to 30 moths per night consider action against eggs few days later and against young larvae 1 to 2 weeks later.
Direct Control: Tie grass to the stems after harvest to gather overwintering larvae and burn grass in spring
In early spring, clean up the old, drying bark of stems with knife and kill the overwintering larvae on bark.
Prune dieback twigs with wilting leaves every third day in flowering period.
Put black light trap (such as from
BYQ company) on the branch about 2 meters high to attract and kill adults during
